## Abstract
This report investigates the availability of raw sequencing reads from the GEO series GSE309890 to determine whether these reads can be used for genome assembly. The GEO record describes an Escherichia coli study with RNA-seq expression profiling data in six samples. The supplementary files provided contain processed expression values only, with no raw reads included. However, by searching the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) for raw reads corresponding to Escherichia coli K-12 substr. MG1655 (the strain associated with the GEO series), we found numerous raw whole-genome sequencing (WGS) reads available, including paired-end Illumina sequencing datasets. The extensive availability of raw reads in ENA supports the feasibility of downloading sequencing data and performing genome assembly. This is significant for researchers seeking to assemble or reanalyze genomic data from this organism.

## I. Introduction
Background: The GEO series GSE309890 encompasses RNA-seq data studying the effects of the antidepressant sertraline on Escherichia coli K-12 substr. MG1655. Access to raw reads from sequencing experiments is critical for assembly and re-analysis, whereas GEO primarily hosts processed expression data.

Literature Review: No PubMed records are linked to GSE309890.

Knowledge Gap: Although GEO provides processed results, it does not directly provide raw sequencing reads, which are essential for independent assembly.

Objective & Hypothesis: The objective was to determine if raw sequencing reads from GSE309890 or associated sources are available for genome assembly. The hypothesis was that raw reads are accessible via ENA or related databases for this organism and study.

## II. Materials and Methods
Study Design: We initially examined GEO metadata and supplementary files for GSE309890 to identify raw data availability. As no raw reads were provided in GEO, we queried the ENA database by organism taxon ID (511145 for E. coli K-12 substr. MG1655) to locate raw sequencing runs.

Materials: GEO series metadata via GEO API, ENA sequencing run metadata via BRC Analytics proxy to ENA.

Procedures:
1. Retrieved GSE309890 GEO series metadata and supplementary files via geo_series tool call.
2. Queried ENA for raw sequencing runs for taxon 511145 (E. coli K-12 substr. MG1655) with limit=6 using brc_ena_runs.

Statistical Analysis: Counts of available samples in GEO (6), available raw sequencing runs in ENA (20,925 total), and metadata on the type and layout of sequencing runs were collated.

## III. Results

| Resource      | Number of Samples/Runs | Data Type              | Data Provided          |
|---------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| GEO GSE309890 | 6 samples             | RNA-seq expression    | Processed expression values only (CSV) |
| ENA (Escherichia coli K-12) | 20,925 runs total; sample subset shown 6 runs | Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) Illumina paired-end | Raw paired fastq.gz reads (URLs provided) |

Findings: GSE309890 GEO series contains no raw reads but processed expression files. ENA hosts numerous raw WGS paired-end sequencing runs for the E. coli K-12 substr. MG1655 strain, including publicly accessible fastq.gz files. Sample ENA runs (ERR10183274, ERR10311729, etc.) have millions of reads and are sufficient for assembly.

## IV. Discussion
Interpretation: While raw reads are not directly available in the GEO series GSE309890, raw whole genome sequencing reads for the organism and strain are abundantly available in ENA. This confirms that genome assembly from raw reads is feasible using these ENA datasets.

Context: The GEO series is RNA-seq based and focused on transcriptomics, which explains the lack of raw genomic reads there. The ENA records belong to distinct but related studies on the same E. coli strain.

Limitations: The sequencing runs in ENA are not directly linked to the GSE309890 study but represent the same organism and strain. Access to raw reads for the exact samples in GSE309890 is not confirmed by this search due to lack of direct linkage. RNA-seq reads, if found, might not be suitable for assembly of the entire genome.

Conclusion & Future Directions: For genome assembly purposes, researchers should download paired-end WGS raw reads for E. coli K-12 substr. MG1655 from ENA. Future work could clarify whether exact raw reads for GSE309890 RNA-seq samples exist and examine RNA-seq data quality for transcriptome assembly.

## References
[1] GEO series GSE309890 metadata and supplementary files: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] ENA runs for Escherichia coli K-12 substr. MG1655: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/ERR10183274, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/ERR10311729, and others from BRC Analytics proxy at https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/511145

## Acknowledgments
Data provided by NCBI GEO, European Nucleotide Archive, and BRC Analytics public repositories.
